response.title: Harborlight FY2027 Budget and a Sixth Site

segments.heading: The request
segments.text: Staff ask the board to approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The money would open a sixth site. The new site would sit in the Eastgate branch library. The budget also adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also say it would cut the waitlist in half. That is the core of the request.

segments.heading: Who Harborlight served
segments.text: In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners at five neighborhood sites. The year before, it enrolled 936. Of this year's learners, 412 worked toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. The results were strong. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. That is the most in the organization's history.

segments.heading: Tutors and staff
segments.text: Harborlight depends on volunteers. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. Tutors also tend to stick around for a while. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight also has paid staff. It employs 11 full-time staff, and four of them are site coordinators. The FY2027 budget would add two more site coordinators. It would also add the sixth site.

segments.heading: Money and reserves
segments.text: Next, the money. FY2026 operating expenses were $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. The cost per learner was $1,237. The treasurer, Dev Patel, flagged one concern. Reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months.

segments.heading: The waitlist
segments.text: Demand still runs ahead of space. At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist. Most of them were at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. On average, they waited nine weeks. Staff estimate the sixth site would cut that waitlist in half. A learner at the Riverside site summed up what is at stake. Quote: "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring." End quote.

segments.heading: What comes next
segments.text: The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21. It also made two requests of staff for that meeting. First, it asked for a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request. Second, board members asked for a short deck. They want to use the deck with funders when they talk about the sixth site. Those are the next steps.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. First, staff ask for an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 to add a sixth site and two site coordinators. Second, demand is high. 287 adults were on the waitlist, and the average wait was nine weeks. Third, reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. That falls short of the board's target of 4 months.
